//: What 'parity init' installs into a consuming repo, and the phases 'parity init --phase-driver' runs. The kit is this folder plus templates/, embedded in the binary; init and doctor read only this file, so adding a skill folder, a hook script or a template needs no code change. Paths are repo-relative with forward slashes; 'from' is a file or a folder of the kit (adopt/... or templates/...).
//install: Owned by the tool: created when missing, reported as differing when they changed, overwritten only by 'parity init --merge'.
//create: Owned by the repo: created once, never touched again (the repo extends them).
//config: The config skeleton: this template with the keys init can derive from the legacy csproj filled in. Created once.
//settings: The hooks block merged into the repo's settings.json: parity's entries are appended after the repo's own, nothing else is touched.
//phases: In order. 'prompt' is what the driver hands the headless agent ({module} and {form} are filled in). 'pause' stops the driver after that phase when more phases were asked for: the step in between is a human's. 'driven: false' keeps the phase valid for .phase but out of the driver (it needs input only a person has).

phases.name: extract
phases.prompt: Run the parity-extract skill for form {form} of module {module}.
phases.pause: record a fixture for every service call listed in legacy/{module}/module.json before the next phase

phases.name: specify
phases.prompt: Run the parity-specify skill for form {form} of module {module}.
phases.pause: review the spec against the running legacy app and set status: reviewed before the next phase

phases.name: implement
phases.prompt: Run the parity-implement skill for form {form} of module {module}.
